items.description: AI model management in Azure HorizonDB is now in limited preview, designed to simplify how you bring AI into your database. With just a single step, you can provision fully managed AI models for embeddings, semantic ranking, and generation through Microsoft Foundry, without having to manage endpoints, credentials, or cross-service configuration.  This integrated experience removes the need for manual setup and context switching, allowing you to use built-in AI functions directly within PostgreSQL and immediately start building AI-powered applications. You also gain a unified environment where model provisioning, management, monitoring, and billing are handled seamlessly within Azure HorizonDB, helping you stay focused on your application logic instead of infrastructure complexity. The same in-database experience extends to existing models you've already deployed in Microsoft Foundry, streamlining registration while providing full integration with AI functions. To request access, complete the AI Model Management limited preview participation form. Learn more.
items.title: Limited Preview: AI model management in Azure HorizonDB

items.description: On February 2, 2027, we will retire Azure Fluid Relay. After this date, Azure Fluid Relay will reach end of availability, and workloads that continue to depend on the service may experience disruption.The Fluid Framework remains available as an open-source framework for building distributed, real-time collaborative web applications. A self-hosted Fluid service solution is available as the replacement. You can continue using Azure Fluid Relay until February 1, 2027 while you complete your transition.How this affects you:If your applications continue to use Azure Fluid Relay after February 2, 2027, they may experience service disruption. Moving to the self-hosted solution means that you will be responsible for hosting and operating the Fluid service in your environment. Operational and infrastructure costs will depend on your deployment architecture, scale, and operational requirements.What you need to do:Transition workloads that depend on Azure Fluid Relay to a self-hosted Fluid service solution before February 2, 2027. Review your Azure subscriptions and identify applications that use Azure Fluid Relay, plan and complete the transition, and use the self-hosted Fluid service solution in the Fluid Framework GitHub repository as the migration and replacement resource.
items.title: Retirement: Azure Fluid Relay

items.description: We're excited to announce the general availability of throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB. You can manage the resource consumption of multiple workloads using the same container by limiting the maximum throughput a workload can consume. You may need to manage workload throughput consumption in scenarios like:Multitenant workloads managed by Independent Software Vendors (ISVs).Bulk execution in ETL jobs.Data ingestion and migration processes.Change feed processing.You can create throughput buckets in a Cosmos DB container using Data Explorer in the Azure portal.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Throughput buckets in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Teams running Windows workloads on AKS often need stronger boot-chain protection for regulated or security-sensitive environments, but Trusted Launch support has historically stopped short of Windows node pools. With Windows Server 2025, AKS will preview Trusted Launch for Windows nodes, adding Secure Boot and vTPM-backed measured boot so the underlying VMs can verify signed boot components and surface boot integrity signals. Platform teams get a more trusted Windows host baseline for Kubernetes workloads, reducing exposure to bootkits, rootkits, and low-level malware without leaving the AKS node pool model.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Windows Trusted Launch

items.description: You can now connect to Azure HorizonDB clusters privately through Azure Private Link, using a private IP address from your virtual network. Private DNS integration makes connection setup easier, while the option to disable public access keeps database traffic off the public internet.   Connections are supported from: Azure virtual networks. Peered networks. On-premises environments through VPN or Azure ExpressRoute.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Private endpoint support for Azure HorizonDB clusters

items.description:
The public preview of Microsoft-managed performance
monitoring for Azure SQL Managed Instance is now available. Customers monitoring business-critical SQL Managed Instance
workloads often rely on custom scripts and disconnected monitoring tools. This
requires them to manage telemetry infrastructure and manually correlate
performance insights across their SQL Managed Instance estate. The new experience collects and stores performance telemetry
and provides resource-level and at-scale dashboards to help identify
performance trends, anomalies, and resource bottlenecks. For deeper analysis
and custom visualizations, you can securely query their monitoring data using
Kusto Query Language (KQL) through an RBAC-protected Azure Data Explorer proxy
endpoint. Learn more:  Documentation Announcement
blog
items.title: Public Preview: SQL performance monitoring for Azure SQL Managed Instance

items.description:
You can now configure backup retention for your Azure HorizonDB deployments from 1 to 35 days, giving you greater flexibility to align backup retention with your application and data protection requirements.  Choose the retention period that best fits your workload and recovery needs while Azure HorizonDB manages backups for you.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Customize backup retention from 1 to 35 days in Azure HorizonDB

items.description:
Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB is now available. You can use geo-redundant backups to strengthen data protection and restore your HorizonDB deployment in another Azure region when needed.  With this capability, you have an additional recovery option for scenarios that require cross-region recovery, helping you improve business continuity and disaster recovery preparedness. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Geo-redundant backup and restore for Azure HorizonDB

items.description: Enhanced Burstable tier (Basv2) builds on the existing burstable model with improved performance predictability and more efficient burst utilization, delivering a better cost-performance balance. Now you can run steady workloads more economically while automatically scaling to handle demand spikes. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL enhanced Burstable tier (Basv2)

items.description: You now have greater flexibility in network design for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server workloads. Now you can change existing VNet-integrated servers from delegated-subnet networking to a private endpoint-capable configuration, enabling secure access over a private IP address through Azure Private Link. The migration retains existing backups; however, you should plan for a temporary connectivity interruption and configure a private endpoint or appropriate firewall rules after migration. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Change from virtual network integration to a private endpoint capable network configuration in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server

items.description: You can now try PostgreSQL 19 in public preview on Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server in the East Asia region. With this preview, you can provision new PostgreSQL 19 servers through the Azure portal and Azure CLI, enabling you to test major version upgrades from supported earlier PostgreSQL versions to PostgreSQL 19. This release gives you early access to PostgreSQL 19 in a fully managed Azure environment and additional time to validate new deployments and upgrade scenarios before general availability. You can test application compatibility, evaluate workloads, and prepare your PostgreSQL estate for broader adoption of PostgreSQL 19.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: PostgreSQL 19 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: User-assigned managed identity (UMI) support is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, enabling you to assign and centrally manage Azure identities for your HorizonDB clusters. With UMI, you can reduce the need to manage credentials for secure access to Azure resources.You can use UMIs with supported HorizonDB capabilities, including customer-managed keys (CMK) and Microsoft Entra authentication, helping you build more secure integrations while reducing the operational burden of managing credentials. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: User-assigned managed identity for Azure HorizonDB

items.description:
Support for .NET
8 and .NET 9 will end on November 10, 2026. Please transition your managed Functions APIs to .NET 10 by that date. Your apps will continue to operate, but security updates
will no longer be provided and support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 on Azure Functions
will end. Running apps on an unsupported runtime or language version might lead
to security and performance issues. Upgrade to .NET 10 before November 10, 2026 to remain on
a supported version. Learn more about the .NET
support policy and the Azure
Functions language support policy. Recommended action To avoid potential security vulnerabilities, minimize
risk for your Azure Static Web Apps managed Functions APIs, and take advantage
of the latest features, act based on your current configuration. If your API currently uses the in-process model  Follow
     the .NET 10 steps in Migrate
     C# apps from the in-process model to the isolated worker model to
     update the API project, packages, startup code, function code, and
     configuration for the isolated worker model.  If your API is already using the isolated worker
model  Follow
     the C# steps in Update
     language versions in Azure Functions to update the API project to
     target net10.0.  For both configurations  Confirm that the API
project targets net10.0, and update the Functions SDK and worker packages
to meet the .NET
10 isolated worker project and package requirements. Build and test the API
locally before continuing.  Set
     the API runtime in staticwebapp.config.json:   {
  "platform": {
    "apiRuntime": "dotnet-isolated:10.0"
  }
}  The API project's TargetFramework and
the platform.apiRuntime value
in staticwebapp.config.json must describe the same runtime. Redeploy your static web app so Azure Static Web Apps rebuilds and publishes the managed API on .NET 10. Complete all required upgrades and ensure your API has moved
off the in-process model before November 10, 2026.  Upcoming change  In November 2026, the default .NET runtime for Azure Static
Web Apps managed Functions APIs will be updated to .NET 10. The
explicit apiRuntime setting in the steps above ensures your app

deployed separately.  Learn
more.
items.title: Retirement: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 on Static Web Apps is ending November 10, 2026

items.description: Microsoft Entra authentication is now generally available for Azure HorizonDB, providing a more secure, identity-based approach to database authentication. You can use Microsoft Entra authentication to centrally manage identities and access instead of relying solely on locally managed database passwords, helping you reduce credential-management overhead and strengthen your security posture.  Microsoft Entra authentication is the recommended authentication approach for HorizonDB. You can use Microsoft Entra authentication exclusively for stronger protection against password-based risks or enable it alongside HorizonDB password authentication when you still require local credentials.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure HorizonDB

items.description: This is the formal notice that Microsoft plans to deprecate the operational technology (OT) security component of Microsoft Defender for IoT. The service will be fully deprecated in October 2029, following a three-year transition period.This change applies only to Defender for IoT OT Security. Enterprise IoT capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint are not affected. Device discovery and vulnerability assessment will continue to be available.When this will happenDeprecation is planned for October 2029. This notice begins the transition period and does not require you to immediately stop using your existing deployment. Complete your migration to an alternative OT security solution before retirement.How this will affect your organizationIf you use Defender for IoT OT Security, you will need to transition to an alternative solution before October 2029. During the transition, the service will remain supported with routine security updates and bug fixes, but no new OT-specific capabilities or feature investments will be introduced. Existing customer agreements and renewals will be honored through October 2029.What you can do to prepareAssess your environment. Review existing OT deployments, sensors, integrations, licenses, contracts, and security requirements.Evaluate your options. Select an OT security solution that meets your organization’s needs. Microsoft offers connectors for Armis, Dragos, and Forescout, but you are not required to use a specific provider. OT data connectors in Microsoft Security Exposure Management support these three providers.Understand Microsoft integrations. Supported third-party OT connectors can bring OT asset and vulnerability data into Microsoft Security Exposure Management and the Defender portal.  Third-party solutions require separate licensing and deployment.Build your transition plan. Account for procurement, testing, operational validation, continuity, data export, and sensor decommissioning, with migration completed before October 2029.Engage early. Contact OT security providers directly or work with your Microsoft account team to help coordinate an introduction.Learn more:OT data connectors Data connectors overview Enterprise IoT
items.title: Retirement: OT security in Microsoft Defender for IoT

items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports centralized
JSON Web Token validation through the AuthPolicy custom resource. Teams can
validate a token signature, issuer, lifetime, and configured audience by using
signing keys retrieved from a trusted HTTPS JSON Web Key Set endpoint. Requests
with missing or invalid credentials are rejected at the gateway instead of
being forwarded to the backend. AuthPolicy can protect an ApplicationLoadBalancer, Gateway,
HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, or MCPRoute. Policies inherit through the resource
hierarchy, while a more specific route-level policy can replace an inherited
policy or explicitly opt a route out. Optional OAuth Protected Resource
Metadata helps OAuth-aware clients discover authorization servers and supported
scopes. Apply consistent JWT
validation to HTTP, gRPC, and MCP routes 
 Use
     Microsoft Entra ID or third-party identity providers that publish trusted
     JWKS signing keys 
 Combine
     JWT validation with WAF so malicious traffic is inspected before
     authentication 
 Publish
     OAuth resource metadata to enable authorization server discovery Learn more: JWT validation for Application Gateway
for Containers Configure JWT validation for
Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API
items.title: Public Preview: JWT validation for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports Model
Context Protocol routing through the new MCPRoute custom resource. Platform
teams can publish MCP servers behind a stable hostname and path while
centralizing TLS, JWT validation, Web Application Firewall protection, backend
health monitoring, and routing policy at the gateway. MCPRoute supports both direct routing to a single MCP
server and aggregation of multiple independent servers behind one logical
endpoint. For aggregated deployments, Application Gateway for Containers merges
tool, resource, and prompt discovery responses, namespaces capability names to
avoid collisions, and routes invocations to the backend that owns the selected
capability. Expose one governed
endpoint for MCP clients and Kubernetes-hosted MCP servers Aggregate capabilities from
multiple MCP servers  Session affinity for MCP
servers that maintain in-memory session state Apply JWT validation, WAF,
backend TLS, health checks, and cross-namespace references Learn more: Model Context Protocol capabilities in
Application Gateway for Containers Configure Model Context Protocol
routing for Application Gateway for Containers
items.title: Public Preview: MCP gateway for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description:
Application
Gateway for Containers now supports private frontends that are reachable only
through approved Azure Private Link private endpoints. This enables
organizations to keep internal applications, shared services, and cross-cluster
traffic on private connectivity while retaining Kubernetes-native Layer 7
routing, TLS, health probing, and Web Application Firewall capabilities. Private ingress supports connectivity across virtual
networks, subscriptions, Microsoft Entra tenants, and Azure regions without
requiring VNet peering. A single Application Gateway for Containers resource
can also host public and private frontends, allowing teams to use separate
exposure models and security policies for different workloads. Remove the public IP
address and direct internet path from the frontend Enforce access through
explicitly provisioned and approved private endpoints  Connect workloads across VNets, subscriptions,
tenants, and regions, including environments with overlapping CIDR ranges  Place an Azure Firewall,
network virtual appliance, or another upstream service in front of Kubernetes
workloads Learn more:   Private ingress with Application
Gateway for Containers  Configure private ingress
with Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API
items.title: Public Preview: Private ingress for Application Gateway for Containers

items.description: The following Azure AI Content Safety preview capabilities will retire on April 30, 2027:Analyze MultimodalCustom categories (rapid), including text and imageConnected containers for Text, Image, and Prompt ShieldsDisconnected containers for Text, ImageEmbedded Content Safety SDKGroundedness detection in Azure AI Content Safety and Azure OpenAIIf you use these capabilities, review the recommended alternatives and plan your migration before the retirement date.Learn more.
items.title: Retirement: Azure AI Content Safety selected features will be retired on April 30, 2027

items.description: Azure Database for MySQL now supports Premium SSD v2 (managed disks) in public preview. Premium SSD v2 provides higher performance and better price-performance compared to Premium File Share, with the flexibility to independently scale storage capacity, IOPS, and throughput. This update enables you to optimize costs and performance based on your workload requirements, from steady-state applications to bursty, transaction-intensive workloads.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for MySQL on Premium SSD v2

items.description: Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB improves search relevance by reordering candidate results based on the meaning of the search text and surrounding context. It uses an AI model to evaluate candidate documents and promote the ones that best match the intent of a query or natural language question, helping you deliver more accurate, context-aware answers in search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) scenarios. With Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB, you can add semantic reranking as a dedicated AI step in retrieval workflows for RAG and agent applications. This helps reduce the need to build and tune custom ranking pipelines while keeping Azure Cosmos DB as the operational data store for search and retrieval experiences.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Semantic Reranker in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB full-text search now includes BM25 score projection, giving you clear visibility into why results appear in the order they do. Your app can now access the relevance score for each result directly, making search ranking more transparent.This new capability helps you display relevance, troubleshoot unexpected ordering, and tune ranking with confidence. You can also compare how different ranking signals contribute to final relevance, helping you build better search experiences on top of your Azure Cosmos DB data.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB full-text search BM25 score projection

items.description: Improved database integration guidance for Azure Managed Redis helps you add caching to applications built with Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure SQL. You can use practical guidance, reference architectures, and step-by-step tutorials to implement caching best practices and common patterns. These resources help you reduce database load, improve application responsiveness, and choose the right caching approach for your workload. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis database integration guidance

items.description: Keyspace notifications are now generally available for Azure Managed Redis, enabling your applications to receive events through pub/sub when data in your cache changes. You can configure the event types that matter to your application and subscribe to notifications for selected keys or operations.  These notifications help you build event-driven applications that monitor key changes, respond to expirations, and trigger downstream actions without continuously polling the cache. You can update the notification settings as your application requirements evolve. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Managed Redis keyspace notifications

items.description: The Azure Managed Redis agent kit makes guidance for building and operating production-ready Redis applications available directly into your AI-assisted development workflows. You get recommendations for caching, messaging, search, AI patterns, client configuration, resilience, and performance, along with Azure-specific guidance for provisioning, networking, security, availability, geo-replication, durability, and observability.  The kit helps you make informed design choices, identify configuration issues earlier, and move from development to production with greater confidence. It also connects you to guided workflows for migrating from Azure Cache for Redis and Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise to Azure Managed Redis.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Managed Redis agent kit

items.description: The general availability of built-in DNS migration tooling simplifies endpoint migration from Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers to Azure Managed Redis. The tooling lets you redirect the existing cache hostname to an existing Azure Managed Redis instance, allowing applications to reconnect using the same hostname and access key. The tool also supports data retention across migration. This built-in tooling reduces immediate application configuration changes and simplifies traffic cutover while you validate the new cache. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cache for Redis to Azure Managed Redis migration tooling

items.description: Azure Managed Redis now supports adding firewall rules for accessing data, and it gives you greater control over network access to your caches. You can restrict connections to approved source IP addresses or Azure service tags, helping protect publicly accessible cache endpoints.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: IP filtering in Azure Managed Redis

items.description: Redis 8 is now available in Azure Managed Redis, bringing the latest Redis innovation to Azure's fully managed Redis service. With richer queries, atomic JSON updates, field-level expiration, and fine-grained security, Redis 8 simplifies development and helps you build sophisticated applications faster. With new vector capabilities, you can build AI-powered applications faster for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, recommendations, and agent memory. Azure Managed Redis helps you move beyond traditional caching and use Redis as a real-time data layer for modern and AI-driven applications. By combining Redis 8 with Azure's enterprise-grade reliability, security, and scalability, you can accelerate application performance, simplify AI architectures, and innovate with confidence on a fully managed service. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Redis 8 in Azure Managed Redis

items.description: Azure Managed Redis now provides shard-level metrics, giving you greater visibility into the performance of individual shards. This added granularity helps you understand workload distribution, identify potential hotspots, and troubleshoot performance more effectively. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Shard-level metrics in Azure Managed Redis

items.description:
Azure Front Door now supports configurable TLS key exchange
policies, including hybrid post-quantum key exchange, to help you prepare for
evolving cryptographic threats while meeting your security and client
compatibility requirements. Choose a predefined Standard or Enhanced policy, or
use a Custom policy to select supported classical and hybrid post-quantum key
exchange groups, including the option to select X25519. Hybrid post-quantum key
exchange requires TLS 1.3 and protects client-to-edge connections; it does not
apply to connections from Azure Front Door to your origin. 

For additional control over TLS encryption,
Azure Front Door also supports disabling the  TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 
cipher suite when TLS 1.3 is configured as the minimum TLS version in TLS
Policy. Together, these updates give you more flexibility to tailor key
exchange and cipher suite settings to your application’s security requirements.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door TLS key exchange policy with post-quantum support

items.description: JSON Web Token (JWT) validation through Azure Front Door Auth Policy is now in public preview on Azure Front Door Premium. Validate bearer tokens issued by Microsoft Entra ID at the edge before requests reach your APIs or web applications, helping you centralize authentication checks and reduce unnecessary traffic to your origins.Associate an Auth Policy with a profile, domain, or route, and configure the expected issuer and audience for token validation. Use Block mode to reject requests with missing or invalid tokens with an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response or evaluate requests without blocking them in Log mode. This preview focuses on validating existing bearer tokens; your application remains responsible for application-specific authorization, and origin access should be restricted to prevent clients from bypassing Azure Front Door.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: JWT validation with Azure Front Door Auth Policy

items.description:
Mutual TLS (mTLS), also known as client certificate
authentication, is now generally available on Azure Front Door Premium. Use
X.509 client certificates to help protect sensitive applications and APIs in
business-to-business, Internet of Things, financial services, and enterprise
scenarios. Choose from four modes: require and validate, require
without validation, validate when presented, or pass through to the origin.
These modes let you control whether client certificates are mandatory and
whether Azure Front Door or your origin performs certificate validation. When
forwarded to the origin, the client certificate is provided in the
X-Azure-ClientCertificate request header. General availability also simplifies trusted CA configuration. You can
upload only the trusted root CA certificate to Azure Key Vault and associate it
with your Front Door custom domain, without uploading intermediate CA
certificates. With this configuration, clients must present their client
certificate and all required intermediate certificates during the TLS
handshake. When edge validation is enabled, Azure Front Door builds and
validates the certificate chain at request time against the configured trusted
root CA.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Front Door mutual TLS authentication

items.description:
Azure
Migrate now supports discovery and assessment for network-attached storage,
allowing customers and partners to plan migrations of Dell PowerScale (OneFS)
and NetApp ONTAP storage to Azure. The Azure Migrate appliance connects
directly to your NAS clusters using read-only credentials, inventories every
SMB, NFS, and S3 share, and evaluates each share against Azure Files, Azure
Blob Storage, and Azure NetApp Files. Key benefits include: Discover Dell PowerScale/Isilon and NetApp ONTAP/FAS clusters
and the shares they host Group, tag, and filter NAS shares alongside your existing
server, application, and database inventory Assess each share with readiness, a right-sized Azure target
configuration, and monthly cost estimates Generate a business case comparing Azure storage services
against on-premises cost, and sequence moves using wave plans This capability replaces manual, spreadsheet-driven
NAS planning with a verified per-share inventory and a defensible cost basis,
especially for large or multi-protocol storage estates. NAS
is often the largest and least-understood part of an on-premises estate.
Bringing NAS discovery and assessment into Azure Migrate means storage is
planned in the same project, and the same business case, as the servers and
applications that depend on it. Getting started: To
get started, update your Azure Migrate appliance, add your NAS cluster as a
discovery source, and run an assessment directly from the Azure portal. Write to us at azurestoragemigrations@microsoft.com with questions or feedback. Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: On-prem NAS share discovery and assessment are now available using Azure Migrate

items.description: You can now restart or fail over databases directly from the Azure portal, including single databases, Hyperscale databases, and databases in elastic pools, without writing scripts against the Rest API or contacting support.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Restart databases in Azure SQL DB via the Azure portal

items.description: You can now use a single Azure SQL Managed Instance link to extend a SQL Server Always On Availability Group with multiple databases to Azure SQL Managed Instance. You can extend an existing availability group or create a new one with multiple databases, providing a simpler path to minimum-downtime migrations and disaster recovery in Azure. With Managed Instance link, you can continuously replicate your databases to and from Azure and perform bidirectional failovers between supported SQL Server versions and Azure SQL Managed Instance. This enhancement streamlines migration and failover for enterprise applications that rely on multiple related databases running together in the same availability group, giving you greater flexibility to migrate, reverse migrate, or set up disaster recovery in Azure while minimizing application disruption.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance link support for availability groups with multiple databases

items.description: Zone redundancy for the Next-gen General Purpose service tier helps improve the resiliency of Azure SQL Managed Instance by distributing critical service components across availability zones. This update helps you protect applications against zonal failures while retaining the performance, scalability, and price-performance benefits of Next-gen General Purpose.   Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Zone-redundant Next-gen GP tier in Azure SQL Managed Instance

items.description: Vaulted backups add an independent protection layer by storing immutable backup copies in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the source Azure Cosmos DB account, and managed through Azure Backup. This update helps you meet a key requirement of many regulated industries.   Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Backup for Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Embedding generation converts content into vector embeddings that capture semantic meaning, helping applications find relevant information beyond exact keyword matches. It uses specialized Azure Data-developed models to support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).  With the Azure.Data.AI SDK, you can add embedding generation directly to retrieval workflows for RAG and agent applications through a focused interface.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Embedding generation in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: The Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Rust gives you a native Rust client for building applications on Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. You get access to database operations directly from Rust, with built-in performance optimizations and failure handling. Efficient binary encoding, automatic retries, and partition-level failover and circuit breaking are enabled by default. These capabilities help you build reliable, high-performance applications with less client configuration and custom recovery logic.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Rust

items.description:
Packet capture Insights uses
AI-assisted analysis to surface key findings from packet captures and can
ingest structured protocol logs into log analytics ingestion for deeper investigation. Packet capture insights help make
capture data more accessible by surfacing meaningful network observations
without requiring you to manually inspect every packet. You can use these
insights to reduce investigation time, identify abnormal behavior, and troubleshoot
connectivity, performance issues more efficiently especially when captures are
large or complex. Optionally ingesting the derived protocol logs
into a Log Analytics workspace preserves structured evidence for deeper
investigation, correlation, validation, and repeatable KQL analysis after the
insight summary is generated.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Packet capture insights

items.description:
Auto scaling introduces a
per-workspace capability in Azure Monitor Workspace (AMW) to automatically
scale ingestion limits based on observed usage patterns. When enabled, the
system dynamically adjusts ingestion limits (quota ceiling) to maintain healthy
utilization and reduce the need for manual limit management. Limits are increased as your metrics volume
grows and can be decreased when usage stays low for a sustained period of time.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Auto scaling of ingestion limits in Azure Monitor workspace

items.description: You can use full-text search in Azure DocumentDB, in public preview, with BM25 indexing, relevance-based sorting, and access to relevance scores. Fuzzy and proximity search help you handle typos and find documents where search terms occur near one another.  With support for additional data types and the compound operator for filtering, you can build more expressive search queries over your document data. These capabilities give you greater control over which results are returned and how they are ranked, without deploying a separate search service.   Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Full-text search in Azure DocumentDB

items.description: DocumentDB for VS Code is now generally available. This free, open-source extension brings Azure DocumentDB and the open-source DocumentDB project into Visual Studio Code, supporting any MongoDB API-compatible workload. You can connect to Azure DocumentDB clusters, Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB accounts, Kubernetes-hosted databases, MongoDB Atlas, or self-hosted servers. Authentication supports Microsoft Entra ID and managed identity. The extension includes a built-in Interactive shell that reuses existing connections, so there is no separate shell to install or configure. You can browse collections; query data in table, tree, or JSON views; use schema-aware autocompletion; and save repeatable scripts in a Query Playground. It also supports DocumentDB Local with Docker and sample data, Query Insights for execution plans and statistics, optional GitHub Copilot recommendations, index management, cluster dashboards, and copy-paste migration of collections and indexes between databases or clusters. Install it from the Visual Studio Marketplace. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: DocumentDB extension for VS Code

items.description: With the public preview of DocumentDB enabled by Azure Arc, you can deploy DocumentDB on supported Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes clusters across on-premises, edge, and multicloud environments. Run MongoDB-compatible document workloads where applications and data need to reside, while using Azure Arc for inventory, configuration, and governance of the underlying Kubernetes infrastructure. Built on PostgreSQL, DocumentDB supports familiar MongoDB-compatible APIs and tools.   Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: DocumentDB enabled by Azure Arc

items.description: With the public preview of DocumentDB on Azure Local, you can run MongoDB-compatible document workloads on your own infrastructure. Deploy applications and their data close together to address latency and data-location requirements in datacenters, retail locations, and industrial environments. Built on PostgreSQL, DocumentDB supports familiar MongoDB-compatible APIs and tools, while Azure Local provides the infrastructure platform.   Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: DocumentDB on Azure Local

items.description: Azure DocumentDB now offers granular role-based access control (RBAC) , well beyond the cluster-level permissions that have been offered in the service. You can now use database-level and collection-level RBAC to manage data access. Instead of relying only on cluster-scoped roles, you can create custom roles for a specific database or individual collection and assign the supported data privileges your users and applications require.  This update gives you greater control over who can access and modify your data, helping you apply least-privilege access across databases, applications, and workloads while keeping permissions scoped to where they are needed.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Fine-grained role-based access control for databases and collections in Azure DocumentDB

New and replacement nodes can reuse model data already cached in the cluster instead of downloading it again from Blob Storage. DACS can also accelerate training workloads that repeatedly read the same portions of a dataset. Performance gains depend on how often data is reused and whether the cache is cold or warm.Enable and manage DACS on your AKS cluster through Azure Container Storage and integrate your workloads using Run:ai Model Streamer, BlobFuse2, or the native Python client. Azure Blob Storage remains the durable source of truth, with clients reading directly from Blob Storage when data isn't cached or the cache is unavailable.Learn

items.description:
AI-summarized connection troubleshoot results introduces a faster, clearer way to understand connectivity test
results in Azure. Connection troubleshoot runs four diagnostic tests, each
giving a different view of the network path. Making sense of these results
together has required strong networking expertise and manual correlation across
tests. With this release, AI does that correlation for customers. AI reviews the results of all four tests together and
returns a single, easy-to-read summary. The summary states what is happening,
the probable cause and how confident the AI is in that cause. It then
recommends next steps to resolve the issue. For example, if all probes to a
destination fail and the diagnostics show no service listening on the tested
port, the summary points to the destination VM as the likely cause. It rates
that finding with high confidence and suggests checking the service status and
port configuration. This enhancement removes the need to interpret and
correlate each test's results by hand. Customers get a clear explanation of
what went wrong and why, along with practical guidance on what to fix. Teams
without deep networking expertise can act on the results themselves, and
experienced engineers can confirm the root cause faster. By adding AI-powered summaries to connection troubleshoot, Azure helps customers move from raw diagnostic data to a
confident, actionable answer in minutes. That makes troubleshooting faster,
simpler and more accessible across their Azure workloads. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – AI summary of connection troubleshoot results

items.description:
Auto-create connection monitor introduces a new, faster way to set up network monitoring across an entire
Azure subscription. Until now, connection monitor tests were created one
connection at a time, with each region, source, destination, test configuration
and alert set up by hand. That approach gives precise control, but setting up
broad coverage takes significant effort. With this release, customers can
choose auto-create next to the existing manual option: select a subscription as
the scope, and Connection Monitor recommends what to monitor. With auto-create connection monitor, the service scans
the subscription's resource topology. It discovers Application Gateways, Load
Balancers, VPN and ExpressRoute gateways, virtual network and local network
gateways, private endpoints and SQL servers. It then recommends the connections
most worth monitoring, skips tests that already exist, and explains the
reasoning behind each recommendation. Customers can review, filter and edit the
recommended tests and see the estimated monthly cost before creating them all
in a single step. Auto-create complements manual setup instead of
replacing it. Customers can use Auto-Create to quickly establish
subscription-wide coverage, and keep creating individual tests manually when
they need fine-grained control over specific connections. This helps teams
reduce blind spots while keeping full transparency and control over every test. By adding auto-create to connection monitor, Azure
gives customers a choice in how they set up monitoring. They can get broad,
reliable coverage in minutes or tailor each test by hand, so connectivity
issues are detected earlier and resolved faster across their Azure workloads. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Auto-create connection monitor

items.description:
Connection analyzer for ExpressRoute Circuit introduces a faster, evidence-based way to find where packet loss
occurs on an ExpressRoute circuit. When customers see packet loss between Azure
and on-premises today, it is often hard to tell whether the problem lies with
the Microsoft Enterprise Edge (MSEE), the connectivity provider, or the
customer's own network. That leads to guesswork and long back-and-forth
investigations. With this release, customers can pinpoint whether the loss originates
at the MSEE. Connection analyzer runs on-demand iPerf test traffic
from an Azure virtual machine to an on-premises destination over the
ExpressRoute circuit, and captures packets at the MSEE. It then reports whether
packet loss is occurring at the MSEE and flags out-of-order packet delivery.
The full packet capture (pcap) is available to download for deeper analysis. This enhancement replaces guesswork with proof. If the
loss is at the MSEE, customers have clear evidence to act on. If it isn't, they
can quickly focus their investigation on the provider or customer side of the
circuit. Built specifically for Azure-to-on-premises traffic, it helps teams
narrow down the source of connectivity issues without lengthy manual analysis. By bringing packet-level visibility to the Microsoft
edge, Azure helps customers isolate ExpressRoute issues faster, shorten time to
resolution, and keep their hybrid workloads running reliably. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Connection analyzer

items.description:
Resource health metrics in connection monitor brings resource health and key performance metrics into the Connection
Monitor test topology, powered by Network Watcher topology. Until now, the
topology showed the path between source and destination, but it didn't show the
health of the resources along that path. When a test reported packet loss or
high latency, customers had to switch between tabs and blades to check each
resource's health and metrics. That slowed down investigations and made it hard
to connect the dots. With this release, health and metrics now appear directly
in the topology. Customers can now click any resource in the connection monitor topology to see its resource health status and time-series metrics in
the same view. For example, selecting a load balancer shows its health along
with data path availability, health probe status, SNAT connection count and SYN count. Customers can view these metrics alongside connection monitor's own
packet loss and latency over the same time window. This makes it easy to see
whether a drop in a resource's health lines up with a connectivity issue. This enhancement brings loss, latency, health and
topology together in one view. When a resource is unhealthy, its metrics are a
click away, with no need to switch tabs or tools. Customers can correlate
resource health signals with connectivity results to reach the root cause
faster. It requires no setup and is available for all new and existing connection monitor tests. By surfacing resource health directly in the connection monitor topology, Azure helps customers go from detecting a
connectivity issue to understanding its cause faster, so they can resolve
problems sooner and keep their workloads running reliably. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Resource health and topology in connection monitor tests

Azure manages and services the Functions host separately while continuing to provide trigger integration, request routing, and event-driven scaling. The preview currently supports .NET isolated, Python, Go, and Node.js, with additional language support planned in the following weeks. Learn more.

items.description: Announcing the GA of smart tier for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage (ADLS) in Azure Government and China regions.Smart tier is a fully managed and automated data tiering solution, avoiding manual tier placement for object storage standard online tiers.   Smart tier automatically moves your data between hot, cool, and cold access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing your costs for these access tiers automatically. New data is stored in the hot tier. Any object that isn’t accessed for 30 days is moved to the cool tier; after 90 days of inactivity, it transitions to the cold tier. If objects are accessed, they are transitioning back to the hot tier and restart their tiering cycle.   Learn more.

items.description: Native cross-database queries in Azure SQL Database Hyperscale let applications access and join data across databases in the same Hyperscale elastic pool on a logical server, using familiar T-SQL three-part names such as `database.schema.object`. This enables cross-database reporting, shared reference data, and remote stored procedure calls without copying data, consolidating databases, or configuring external tables. Importantly, it unblocks SQL Server migration scenarios that depend on cross-database queries, reducing the need for query rewrites and application redesign when moving to Azure SQL Database. Applications retain separate databases with permissions enforced in each, while transactions can read across multiple databases and write to one database per transaction.This capability is available in a limited preview, and customers must sign up to participate.Learn more.

actions (serverless compute at the edge). With edge actions, customers can execute lightweight
JavaScript functions during Azure Front Door client request/response processing
to make real-time decisions closer to users, improving performance, security,
and application flexibility without adding complexity to origin infrastructure. Common scenarios include A/B testing, canary deployments,

items.description:
Azure Application Gateway advanced routing rules is now available in public preview. Advanced routing rules enables you to create flexible, condition-based routing logic using HTTP
request attributes, extending Application Gateway routing beyond traditional
path-based routing. You can define routing
conditions based on HTTP headers, query strings, client IP addresses, HTTP
methods, and request paths, and route matching requests to different backend
pools. Rules support priority-based evaluation, exact-value and pattern matching,
and default routing when no rule matches. Advanced routing rules enables
scenarios such as A/B testing and canary deployments, API versioning,
multi-tenant applications, traffic segmentation, and routing requests to
different application backends based on request characteristics. Learn
more.

items.description: Now the M10 to M30 computer tiers are available for near-instant provisioning.   Historically, the free tier in Azure DocumentDB was made available for instant provisioning. The goal was to help you get started without having to wait for 10-15 minutes for clusters to become available. In addition, AI agents don’t have to spend cycles waiting for cluster provisioning before you can kick off a wave of experimentation.  Now you and your agents can use the popular M10 tier for basic functional testing and experimentation. You can continue to use the M30 as the staple entry point for production-tier applications as you begin your journey on Azure DocumentDB before scaling to higher clusters tiers as you grow.   Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Near-instant provisioning for Azure DocumentDB clusters

items.description: You can now send a query to any node in a multi-shard Azure DocumentDB cluster. The node can handle the query locally or route it to the shard or shards that contain the data. In effect, the nodes in a multi-shard cluster function as a router, being fully shard aware, with the ability to either serve the requests locally, route the request to the appropriate shard containing the data, or route a query across multiple shards, gather the results, and present them as one.  This optimization guarantees performance regardless of the number of shards in a cluster and the size of the shards. For both 1x and 100x of steady state request volume, querying from any node ensures consistent performance at any scale.   Previously, request routing relied on a single coordinator. Now, every node can route requests to the appropriate shards.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB elasticity—query from any node

The platform provisions and manages the hosting infrastructure and provides Microsoft Entra ID authentication, access controls, monitoring integration, and more. This helps teams focus on the tools and data their agents need rather than the operational work of hosting remote MCP servers. Connector Namespace brings two new features to hosted MCP: Bring-your-own container image and a ready-to-deploy Azure Cosmos DB MCP server:Bring your own image: Host a custom MCP server. Managed connectors, provided through the Azure Connector Namespace, wrap service-specific APIs and handle authentication, webhooks, retries, and more, so developers can focus on their application logic while Azure manages the underlying connections and integration infrastructure.Developers can build with C#, Python, and Node.js and use connector triggers together with strongly typed Connector SDK clients for a wide range of services including Outlook, SharePoint, and Dataverse, as well as Salesforce, ServiceNow, and many other third-party systems. Functions support both webhook and polling trigger models with automatic scaling, giving developers flexibility in how applications receive and process events.Managed connectors work alongside existing Azure Functions triggers and bindings, so developers can add integrations incrementally to new or existing applications. While RSA may remain secure against today’s classical computing capabilities, advances in quantum computing could eventually pose a risk. AES-256 keys are considered more resistant to known quantum-computing threats than current asymmetric algorithms such as RSA. This update helps you build greater crypto agility into your platform and take practical steps toward post-quantum readiness.  Learn more.

items.description: Customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest are now available in public preview for Azure HorizonDB.   By default, Azure HorizonDB uses service\-managed keys (SMK) to encrypt data at rest, with Azure managing the encryption keys on your behalf. With CMK, you can instead control the key encryption key (KEK) used to protect your data by managing it in your own Azure Key Vault or Azure Key Vault Managed HSM.  CMKs provide greater control over your encryption key lifecycle and can help you meet your organization’s security and compliance requirements. With CMK, you can: Control access to encrypted data, including revoking key access to make the Azure HorizonDB database inaccessible. Manage the key lifecycle, including key rotation, in accordance with your organization’s compliance policies. Centrally manage and organize encryption keys in Azure Key Vault. Support separation of duties across security officers, database administrators, and system administrators.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Encryption at rest with customer-managed keys in Azure HorizonDB

more.

Once created, the knowledge graph enables applications to answer multi-hop questions that are difficult to resolve through keyword or vector search alone, such as how customers, transactions, incidents, assets, or documents are connected. You can combine semantic retrieval with graph relationships to build more contextual recommendations, accelerate investigations and root-cause analysis, and return traceable evidence explaining how an answer or conclusion was reached. items.description:
Azure HorizonDB introduces substantial Apache AGE performance improvements for querying and building knowledge graphs. Enhanced query planning and optimized graph joins accelerate eligible read queries, while faster duplicate detection and improved memory management make ingestion using `MERGE` more efficient.Benchmark results include: Up to 3,900× faster short
graph lookups: In LDBC SNB tests with approximately 9 million vertices and 53
million edges, listing a person’s friends improved from approximately 1.8
seconds to 0.46 milliseconds. Selected complex queries improved by up to 512×. About 190× faster `MERGE`
ingestion: Processing one million inputs with 100,000 distinct vertices
improved from 906 seconds to 4.8 seconds. 83% lower sampled peak
backend memory usage: In a separate 10-million-input test, memory usage fell
from approximately 65.2 GiB to 11.0 GiB. Both read-query optimizations are enabled by default.
Statistics-aware property estimates require explicitly creating property
statistics and running `ANALYZE`. Performance gains vary by query, dataset, and
configuration. Learn more.

items.description:
Announcing the public preview
of rate limit grouping for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front
Door Premium. By default, a rate limit rule counts requests separately for
each client IP address. Distributed attacks get around this by spreading their
traffic across thousands of IP addresses, so that each one stays under the
threshold. Rate limit grouping adds new group-by options that count requests by
an attribute those clients share, so traffic from many IP addresses counts
toward a single threshold.  With this preview, you can group each rate limit rule by: JA4 fingerprint, to limit
attacks that rotate through many IP addresses but reuse the same client
software. AS number, to cap traffic
from networks your users don't usually come from, such as hosting and cloud
providers, without maintaining lists of their IP ranges. Country/region, to cap the
traffic that any single country or region can send. You can also choose None to count all requests that match a
rule together, for example to cap the total request rate to a sign-in page.
Existing rate limit rules keep counting requests per IP address, so nothing
changes until you choose a grouping. Configure grouping in the Azure portal,
ARM templates, Bicep, the REST API, or Azure PowerShell, and keep a per-IP rule
alongside your grouped rules. Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Rate limit grouping for Azure Front Door Premium WAF

items.description:
Session-based authentication is now in public preview
for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage.Session-based
authentication reduces the per-request authentication and authorization time
for AI agents and applications while preserving the security controls
organizations already rely on.With
session-based authentication, an agent or application authenticates once with
Microsoft Entra ID, establishes a short-lived session for a container, and uses
that session for subsequent reads.Session-based
authentication provides three benefits:Improved
     performance. Identity
     and permissions are verified once when the session is created. Subsequent
     read requests to the container use that session which reduces per-request
     authentication and authorization latency.The
     same least privileged access, now short-lived. Sessions use your organization’s
     existing permission model for least privileged access, Azure RBAC and
     Azure ABAC. Each session is also scoped to one container, expires after
     five minutes, is bound to the client that created it, and requires every
     request to be signed.Full traceability.  Azure Storage diagnostic logs currently record the Microsoft Entra
ID identity behind each request, and the same is true with sessions. With
sessions, every request remains tied to the Microsoft Entra ID identity that
created the session, so security teams keep visibility into which identity,
human or agent, accessed what data, and when. This preview
is available in all public regions, supports the Get Blob operation, and is
available through the REST API and Azure Storage SDKs. With the SDK, enabling
session-based authentication is a single client configuration option, with no
changes to your application logic.Creating a
session is billed as a write transaction. Read requests made with a session are
billed at the standard transaction rates for your storage account type.Learn more: Blog  Documentation
items.title: Public Preview: Session-based authentication for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage

items.description:
Azure Adaptive Virtual Patching
introduces an AI-orchestrated Adaptive Shield designed to reduce exposure to
new, emerging, and newly disclosed zero-day vulnerabilities while customers
test and deploy software patches. The initial workload focus is Linux Virtual Machines
(VM) and Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) on Azure. The service connects three semantic layers: a knowledge graph of
vulnerabilities and exploit conditions, a map of the customer’s actual
workloads and runtime context, and an orchestration layer that identifies
relevant exposure and generates workload-specific mitigations. AI-synthesized
policies use explicit matching conditions and enforcement actions, combining
adaptive reasoning with deterministic runtime enforcement. The Adaptive Shield
architecture coordinates eBPF-based workload protection and network-based
compensating controls to address relevant attack paths. Customers onboard workloads as Protected Resources. A workload
extension collects telemetry and deploys mitigations directed by the service’s
AI core, helping protection adapt as threats and workload conditions change.
Azure Adaptive Virtual Patching complements existing security investments and
gives customers time to patch safely. It applies temporary mitigations rather
than installing software fixes; the corresponding mitigations can be rolled
back after patching and confirmed remediation. Learn more:DocumentationAnnouncement blog

blog

Resiliency drift detection, resource and application monitoring, and built-in drills help you proactively maintain their resiliency posture, validate recoverability, and support compliance reporting. You can additionally leverage the Resiliency Agent (preview) to automatically discover application boundaries and access ready-to-run remediation scripts.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager

items.description:
Azure SRE Agent can now take part in Microsoft Teams
conversations in public preview. Engineers can start an investigation, follow
up on findings, and work with the agent in one-on-one chats, group chats,
channels, and meeting chats without leaving Teams. When an action requires
authorization, the agent posts an approval card in the conversation. Administrators decide which shared conversations the agent
can take part in, while existing tool policies determine whether actions are
allowed, require approval, or are denied. Microsoft Entra Agent ID enables the
agent’s Teams presence; managed identity and Azure role-based access control
continue to govern access to Azure resources. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Teams integration for Azure SRE Agent

items.description:
Azure SRE Agent now supports the open Agent-to-Agent (A2A)
protocol in public preview. SRE agents can hand tasks to other agents and
accept tasks from them while each agent retains its own team’s permissions. For
example, an application team’s agent investigating a latency spike can ask a
database team’s agent to check query performance and bring the findings back
into the same investigation. Administrators determine which agents an SRE agent can call,
approve incoming callers in the same Microsoft Entra tenant, and select which
custom agent handles their requests. Connections use managed identity and do
not give remote agents direct access to the caller’s tools or permissions. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol support in Azure SRE Agent

items.description:
Azure SRE Agent now supports Microsoft Entra Agent ID and
Microsoft Agent 365 in public preview, so security and IT teams can see and
govern SRE agents alongside other agents in the organization. Each agent can have its own Agent ID in addition to its
managed identity. Teams can assign Azure roles to the Agent ID so the agent's
actions appear as itself in Entra and in Azure activity logs. Through Agent
365, administrators can find SRE agents in the tenant's agent registry and
monitor their activity with Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Agent 365 for Azure SRE Agent

items.description:
Azure SRE Agent is coming to Slack in
private preview. Organizations that coordinate incident response in Slack can
work with the agent in the channels where responders already work, mentioning

items.title: Private Preview: Slack integration for Azure SRE Agent

items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection custom policy is now generally
available, and it’s one of our most requested features. By default,
machine-learning auto-tuning sets detection thresholds for each protected
resource, which works well for most workloads. But latency-sensitive apps,
high-throughput services, and gaming or event-driven workloads with planned
spikes often need a fixed threshold. Custom policy lets you set your own for
individual protocols, across Azure resources with public IP endpoints, on both
Network Protection and IP Protection SKUs. Each policy holds one or more rules that define a protocol
(TCP, UDP or TCP SYN), an inbound direction, and a packets-per-second threshold
that triggers mitigation. You can link a policy to up to 1,000 resources, and
you can create it first and add associations later. Setting a threshold turns
off auto-tuning for that protocol only, so everything else stays
machine-learning tuned. Settings now persist with your resource, so they
survive workload removal or VM shutdown, and you manage them yourself without
on-call support. Take control of how your workloads are protected. Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure DDoS Protection custom policy

items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection now
covers the public IPs behind Azure NAT Gateway StandardV2, in public preview.
You can protect the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses that carry your outbound internet
traffic from network-layer DDoS attacks, using the same DDoS Network Protection
or IP Protection you already have. There’s no new API, feature registration or
appliance to manage, and no unsolicited inbound connections are opened to your
gateway. Why it matters: NAT Gateway doesn’t accept inbound
connections, but its public IPs are still reachable from the internet, and
they’re the identity of everything behind them. Partners, SaaS providers and
banks often allow-list these IPs, so anyone who learns them can aim traffic at
them. Every VM in the associated subnets shares the same IPs, so a single flood
can cut off API calls, partner integrations, updates and telemetry all at once.
An attacker doesn’t need to reach your workloads to cause an outage, only to
break their path to the internet. Now your outbound IPs get
automatic network-layer mitigation, plus the DDoS metrics, diagnostics and
alerts you already rely on. It also simplifies compliance, because policies
requiring DDoS protection on all public IPs no longer need an exception for NAT
Gateway. Learn
more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection support for NAT Gateway v2 IP

items.description: Running AI agents that execute untrusted, model-generated code requires isolated environments for each session. Today, teams building on Kubernetes assemble their own sandbox lifecycle, storage, and warm-up logic, adding operational overhead and making users wait while fresh environments initialize.  We’re introducing the Agent Sandbox cluster extension. Built on the open-source Kubernetes Agent Sandbox project, the managed extension provides declarative sandbox creation, lifecycle management, and pre-warmed pools. Together, Agent Sandbox cluster extension and Pod Snapshot cluster extension enable isolated agent environments to be snapshotted and restored while preserving runtime state across the sandbox lifecycle.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agent Sandbox cluster extension

items.description: Restarting a sandboxed workload means losing in-memory state and repeating costly initialization. AI environments must reload models and rebuild runtime context; other sandboxed applications must repeat Java Virtual Machine (JVM) warmup or repopulate caches. Users wait while work that was already completed runs again. We’re introducing the Pod Snapshot cluster extension to capture a supported pod runtime state and restore it on demand, preserving memory and process state in Azure Blob instead of cold-starting. Paired with the Agent Sandbox cluster extension, it lets teams capture and restore isolated agent environments. For both agent and other supported sandboxed workloads, resuming from captured state reduces repeated initialization and the wait before work can continue. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Pod snapshot cluster extension

Instead of managing multiple independent ExpressRoute connections, you can aggregate multiple physical links into a single logical connection.With link groups, you can:Scale connectivity capacity by grouping multiple ExpressRoute Direct links into a single logical connection.Improve resiliency with Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP), including dynamic link negotiation and failover.Simplify operations by managing aggregated connectivity and monitoring at the group level instead of operating independent connections.Customize availability behavior by configuring the minimum number of active links required for the group to remain operational.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Scale ExpressRoute Direct connectivity with link groups

Agent now natively supports AWS and Google Cloud through built-in connectors,

guide   Google Cloud
connector guide

items.description: Isolated pods should not force a tradeoff between security and startup performance. With classic sandboxed pod flows, every pod boots a new Kata VM, which adds cold-start latency and extra memory overhead before your app begins work.The new kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class changes that default. It creates pods from a pre-initialized sandbox VM template instead of booting each sandbox from scratch, reduces per-pod memory overhead, and uses Kata’s Rust runtime for better efficiency. You keep strong pod-level VM isolation while getting faster starts and lower runtime cost for sandboxed workloads.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Pod Sandboxing kata-vm-isolation-v2 runtime class

items.description: Regulated customers running AKS Confidential VM node pools protect workloads in memory today, but the OS disk isn't encrypted at rest, so they have to close the data-at-rest gap outside the platform. In Preview, Ubuntu 26.04 Confidential VM node pools enable OS Disk Encryption by default on both Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP SKUs, so the OS disk is protected with a CVM-bound key from first boot. Confidential workloads get end-to-end confidentiality (memory and OS disk) without new configuration, new API surface, or changes to existing tooling.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Confidential VMs with OS Disk Encryption support on AKS

items.description: Customers standardized on Intel Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) for attestation and hardware confidentiality can't run those workloads on AKS Confidential VM node pools today, because CVM node images only support AMD SEV-SNP. AKS Confidential VM node pools add Intel TDX support alongside AMD SEV-SNP, and the correct CVM image is selected automatically from the VM SKU. Intel-first customers can now bring their confidential workloads to AKS without changing their attestation model, and without any new AKS configuration or API surface. Generally available with Azure Container Linux. Supported with Ubuntu 26.04 preview.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Confidential VMs with Intel TDX support on AKS

items.description: Azure Linux 4.0 is being introduced as part of Microsoft Ignite. The general availability of Azure Linux 4.0 for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets is Microsoft's first-party open-source Linux distribution purpose-built for Azure. It brings a modernized stack — including Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, dnf5 package manager, glibc 2.42, OpenSSL 3.5, and Python 3.14 — optimized for Azure compute, storage, and networking. It delivers faster VM startup and provisioning with a reduced package footprint and a security-first design.  Key highlights: Azure-tuned kernel — Linux 6.18 LTS with improved Hyper-V integration, GPU/AI accelerator support, and new hardware drivers Secure by default — Secure Boot, Trusted Launch, SELinux support, kernel hardening, and SBOMs published with target SLSA Level 3 Minimal footprint — Ships only the packages required for cloud workloads, reducing attack surface from day one No additional OS licensing cost — Included with Azure compute; no separate OS licensing fees or support contracts Microsoft-owned supply chain — From kernel to CVE response, enabling fast-track Critical/High CVE patches with monthly security updates Predictable lifecycle —full support with LTS kernel and annual HWE kernel updates for new hardware platforms Container images — Base, and distroless images available on Microsoft Container Registry (MCR)Learn more: Ignite 2026 blog GitHub Documentation
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Linux 4.0

system-managed maintenance for planned service upgrades.With system-managed

items.description:
Azure DDoS Protection peacetime telemetry is now in public
preview. Customers can now see the traffic reaching their protected public IP
addresses during normal operation, not only while a DDoS mitigation is active. Previously, outside an active mitigation, a protected public
IP address showed only its mitigation-trigger metrics. With peacetime
telemetry, the existing incoming DDoS traffic metrics (total, TCP, SYN, UDP and
other traffic) show data during normal operation. Customers can use this data to understand normal traffic
patterns, compare everyday traffic with mitigation triggers, create Azure
Monitor metric alerts with workload-specific thresholds, and test dashboards
and alerts without simulating an attack. Peacetime telemetry works automatically for public IP
addresses protected by DDoS Network Protection or DDoS IP Protection, with no
registration and no new metric names. Viewing the metrics doesn't require Log
Analytics or diagnostic settings, and protection and mitigation behavior don't
change. There's no additional cost beyond existing DDoS Protection pricing;
standard Azure Monitor charges apply to alert rules. During the preview,
peacetime telemetry is available in the Azure public cloud. Learn more: Read
about peacetime telemetry availability Set
up traffic-condition alerts during peacetime
items.title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection peacetime telemetry

Azure Policy provides a centralized way to define and enforce organizational

more.

items.description: Project NOVA enables independent verification of specific claims without revealing the underlying data. Across regulated industries, organizations need to establish trust while protecting confidential information. Project Nova explores how zero-knowledge proofs can enable privacy-preserving transactions, interoperability, and regulatory assurance across organizational boundaries. In financial services, zero-knowledge proofs could enable cross-chain settlement by verifying transaction conditions across networks, support selective disclosure of sensitive information, and provide regulators with independent assurance of compliance without exposing underlying records. Beyond financial services, healthcare organizations could verify patient eligibility without sharing medical histories; AI systems could prove defined computations without exposing sensitive inputs; and supply chains could demonstrate compliance or product provenance without revealing confidential supplier relationships.
items.title: Private Preview: Project Nova

items.description: Azure's next-generation confidential VMs, the DCasv7, DCadsv7, DCalsv7, DCaldsv7, ECasv7 and ECadsv7 series, are now in private preview. Built on 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors with AMD SEV-SNP, they protect data while it's being processed by isolating each VM in hardware from the hypervisor, host operators and other tenants. Customers can move sensitive, regulated workloads to the cloud without changing their code. General-purpose, low-memory and memory-optimized sizes are available, with or without local disk, so customers can match price and performance to each workload while meeting privacy, compliance and sovereignty requirements.
items.title: Private Preview: Azure confidential VMs on 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors (DCasv7 and ECasv7 series)

items.description: Azure Workload Center for SAP, together with the Azure Copilot Run SAP Agent, is a workload-aware experience, powered by Workload Virtual Instance (WVI) for operating SAP workloads on Azure. Azure Workload Center for SAP helps teams understand workload health, identify configuration deviations, and assess the impact of platform issues in the context of the SAP systems they support.Each workload is represented as a Workload Virtual Instance (WVI), bringing architecture, dependencies, metadata, and operational context into a single view. Workload-specific details, such as SAP system identifiers (SIDs) and production designations, help teams and AI agents understand each environment in context, while Azure Monitor health models provide health insights across application, database, and infrastructure layers. Customers can discover and onboard workloads, validate configurations against SAP-specific best practices, detect deviations, monitor health, troubleshoot issues, and take guided remediation actions. Purpose-built AI agents help operators understand what changed, assess impact, and identify recommended next steps while keeping teams in control of decisions and remediation. Availability: Australia East, Central US, East US, East US 2, Germany West Central, Italy North, Japan East, Korea Central, North Europe, South Central US. To sign up for this Limited Preview, please fill out this form.  Learn more: Limited Preview of Microsoft Azure Workload Center for SAP | Tech Community Blog Azure Workload Center for SAP | Microsoft Learn

items.description: Sovereign Control Panel is now available in Public Preview. Sovereign Control Panel is an Azure portal experience designed to help organizations assess and continuously monitor their sovereignty posture, understand the evidence behind identified gaps, and take guided action to address them. From a centralized experience, customers can apply sovereignty controls, prioritize remediation recommendations, and track improvements across their existing Azure estate, reducing the need to manually assemble information across tools and teams for each assessment. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Sovereign Control Panel

items.description: The Production Touch Ledger (PTL) Assessment Report is now available. Capgemini, an independent third party, has validated the design of PTL for its ability to preserve the completeness, tamper-evidence, and non-repudiation of production-access records. This provides customers with independent assessment of PTL’s capabilities rather than solely relying on Microsoft’s claims. PTL, launched with phased rollout in the EU Data Boundary, provides organizations a verifiable record of when and how Microsoft personnel access the in-scope production systems that host their workloads. Every access record is written to Azure Confidential Ledger, making the record tamper-evident: once an entry is recorded, any attempt to alter or remove it can be detected. Security, compliance, and risk teams can use the PTL Assessment Report as independent evidence in regulatory reviews, internal audits, and customer access conversations.Learn more:Download the Assessment ReportProduction Touch Ledger Documentation
items.title: Announcing: Production Touch Ledger (PTL) Assessment Report
