Access is subject to monitoring by authorized EU-resident personnel from a trusted partner. With this update, customers reviewing their sovereignty posture in Sovereign Control Panel can learn about Data Guardian, understand how it supports their access oversight requirements, all from the same centralized experience. This makes it easier to move from assessing posture to exploring relevant controls, without searching across separate tools and documentation. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Discover Data Guardian from Sovereign Control Panel

items.description: Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks is an open-source command-line tool that you run inside compatible Azure VMs. Backed by Azure Boost, the tool provides remote disk I/O and latency metrics and maps each disk inside your VM to the corresponding disk shown in the Azure portal. This helps you investigate remote disk performance and associate metrics with the right disk.Learn more.
items.title: Announcing: Azure Boost observability for NVMe disks

items.description: VM adaptive placement, now in public preview, helps increase Azure VM deployment success when capacity is constrained.With a standard VM create, you specify one exact size, and the deployment fails if that size isn't available. With adaptive placement, you specify a preferred size instead. Azure deploys your preferred size when it can. If it isn't available, Azure deploys a compatible alternative with the same vCPU count, the same or newer generation, and equivalent performance.Adaptive placement isn't a new VM type or pricing offer. You get a regular Azure VM, billed at standard rates for the deployed size, with no additional charge.Key capabilities:Replace custom retry loops and fallback lists with a placement decision Azure makes at request timeSee both your preferred size and the deployed size on the VMUse it for new VMs or update existing VMsDuring preview, preferred sizes can come from the D-, E- and F-series families. Adaptive placement is for single VMs and isn't supported with Capacity Reservations, Dedicated Hosts, Availability Sets or Proximity Placement Groups. It works within your quota and isn't a capacity guarantee. Use the REST API, Azure PowerShell or the .NET and Python SDKs; the Azure portal isn't supported in preview.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: VM adaptive placement

items.description: Azure Artifact Validation, in public preview, lets VM image publishers and enterprise platform teams run Azure's certification-grade quality and security checks on their images in their own Azure subscriptions, at any point in the build process.Previously, these checks ran only when you submitted an Azure Marketplace offer in Partner Center. Now you can validate Windows and Linux images bound for Azure Marketplace, galleries or other distribution platforms, and find issues while they're still inexpensive to fix.Key capabilities:Self-service validation runs in your own subscription, with your choice of tests and timingChecks for bootability, OS configuration and platform compatibility, plus malware and vulnerability scanning powered by Microsoft DefenderA native Azure resource with an API, so you can add validation to CI/CD pipelines as a release gatePer-test results with stable error codes and clear reasonsArtifact Validation complements Azure Marketplace certification and doesn't replace it; final certification still runs through Partner Center.Available in Central US, North Central US, South Central US, Sweden Central, Japan East and Australia East through the REST API, ARM templates and Azure SDKs.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Artifact Validation for VM images

items.description: Zone resilience for Azure VMs, now in public preview, lets you recover an eligible zonal VM in another availability zone in the same region, retaining the existing VM resource and configuration.ZRS managed disks replicate data synchronously across zones but don't restart an affected VM. Zone resilience reuses supported disks and configuration, with a near-zero recovery point objective (RPO) for data committed to disks.Key capabilities:Change zone placement without creating a new VM resourceRecover with existing OS and data disks rather than restoring copiesChoose the target zone and when recovery startsZone resilience is a customer-initiated recovery option, not automatic failover. Recovery involves downtime and depends on available capacity in the target zone. Enable it while the source zone is healthy, on a standalone zonal VM that uses Premium SSD ZRS or Standard SSD ZRS for the OS disk and every data disk. The preview doesn't support Virtual Machine Scale Sets, On-demand Capacity Reservations, Azure Site Recovery or write-accelerated data disks. It provides in-region recovery and doesn't replace regional disaster recovery or multi-zone high availability designs. Use the preview for evaluation and testing with nonproduction VMs.
items.title: Public Preview: Zone resilience for Azure VMs

items.description: Bring your existing Agent2Agent (A2A) agents to Agent Service without a protocol conversion layer.Previously, Agent Service converted incoming A2A requests to the Responses protocol. With A2A passthrough, Agent Service forwards native A2A requests directly to your hosted agent container. Your code handles A2A messages and tasks. Agent Service manages the endpoint, authentication, and hosted compute.The preview supports incoming A2A v1.0 requests over JSON-RPC. items.description:
Immutable snapshots for Azure Disk Storage are now available in public preview. Immutable snapshots complement Azure Backup immutable vaults. Use vaults for cost-efficient long-term retention, and immutable snapshots for short-term backups that need faster restore. Snapshots are read-only after creation, and you can apply an immutability policy to existing snapshots of any Azure disk type to prevent deletion for up to 90 days. While the policy is active, no one can delete the snapshot, regardless of role or permissions. This helps protect your backups from accidental or malicious deletion and supports regulatory data retention requirements. You can still restore disks, copy snapshots to other regions, and perform all other snapshot operations. Choose between two types of immutability policies: Unlocked policies let authorized users test a policy before locking it. Authorized users can extend, shorten, or remove an unlocked policy.Locked policies provide compliance-grade protection. They can only be extended. No one, including administrators and Azure, can shorten or remove them, so the snapshot can't be deleted until the retention period ends. Use them to protect backups from ransomware, meet regulatory requirements for short-term backups that need fast restore, and guard against rogue AI agent behavior.There's no additional charge for immutability policies; protected snapshots continue to be billed at standard managed disk snapshot rates until you delete them. Learn more:

Announcing the public preview
of the AI bot ruleset for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front
Door Premium. AI crawlers and agents visit your site for different reasons,
and you may want to allow some but not others. Robots.txt only works when a bot
chooses to follow it, and some bots pretend to be a well-known AI crawler. The
AI bot ruleset identifies AI bots, groups them by purpose, and enforces your
choice for each group at the edge. With this preview, you can choose an action for each of four
categories: AI training, for verified
crawlers that collect public content to train or fine-tune AI models. AI search, for verified
crawlers that index content to power AI search, answers, and summaries. AI interactive agents, for
verified agents that fetch pages in real time when a person asks an AI
assistant. Miscellaneous AI agents,
for AI bots that can't be verified, including bots that falsely claim to be a
well-known AI crawler. Microsoft keeps the AI bot
signatures up to date, with no ruleset version change needed. Every rule starts
with the Log action, so you can review your AI bot traffic in WAF logs and WAF
insights before anything is blocked. You can set each category to Allow, Block,
Log, JS challenge, or CAPTCHA, and configure the ruleset in the Azure portal,
Azure PowerShell, Azure CLI, or Bicep. Learn
more.

items.description: Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation is now in public preview. Elastic SAN Next Generation keeps the core benefits customers value in Elastic SAN today: a single SAN resource hierarchy to consolidate block storage workloads and dynamically share performance, simplifying storage management and lowering total cost of ownership at scale. As a cloud SAN offering, Elastic SAN supports SAN migrations such as datacenter exits and hardware refreshes through iSCSI connectivity, along with the scale needed for cloud-native workloads.Next Generation builds on that foundation to support mission-critical workloads and advanced storage capabilities such as thin provisioning and autoscaling, helping customers further optimize storage costs while expanding Elastic SAN's fit across SAN migrations and cloud-native applications.Run mission-critical and general-purpose workloads on the same SAN with noisy-neighbor protection.Quality of service (QoS) tiers at the volume-group level let customers match performance to workload requirements:Business Critical: Reserved performance with low sub-millisecond latency, up to 400,000 IOPS and 10,000 MBps per volume. Built for SAP HANA, Epic, and I/O-intensive OLTP.General Purpose - Direct Attach: Shared performance with sub-millisecond latency, up to 80,000 IOPS and 2,000 MBps per volume. Built for vector and OSS databases.General Purpose - iSCSI: Shared performance with low single-digit millisecond latency, up to 80,000 IOPS and 1,280 MBps per volume. Built for external storage needs such as Azure VMware Solution (AVS) or customers who prefer iSCSI connectivity.Efficient provisioning for lower storage TCOProvision for workload growth without paying for the full logical capacity of volumes upfront, while scaling capacity and performance independently:Thin provisioning: Size volumes for anticipated growth while consuming physical capacity as data is written, up to 5x the SAN's provisioned capacity.Autoscaling: Automatically add SAN capacity based on customer-defined thresholds.Independent capacity and performance provisioning: Provision capacity, IOPS, and throughput independently at the SAN level.Thin clones (coming soon): Create space-efficient, mountable dev/test copies of Business Critical volumes.Crash-consistent snapshots: Protect volumes with point-in-time snapshots.A Next Generation SAN can scale up to 1 PiB, 4 million IOPS, and 160 GBps. Sign up for Azure Elastic SAN Next Generation preview.

items.description: Programmed Training, an API for building your own post-training loop over open-weight models, is available in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. Access is available by request through the preview sign-up form.Managed training jobs work well when you only need to choose a dataset, a grader or job settings. Research teams that need a custom learning signal or control over each update have had to run and maintain their own GPU training infrastructure.With Programmed Training, your Python program controls the experiment while Foundry runs sampling and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) updates on serverless GPUs. Your code decides how rollouts are collected, how rewards and advantages are computed, which tokens contribute to learning, and when to apply each optimizer update. The same building blocks support reinforcement learning, supervised learning, preference learning, distillation and custom-loss workflows. You can save adapter and optimizer state and resume training in a compatible session.Learn more.

items.description: Multi-turn evaluation is now in public preview in Microsoft Foundry. You can assess complete agent conversations against your quality standards, not only individual responses.A response can look correct on its own and still be part of a conversation that fails the user. For example, an agent can repeat the same failing action across several turns and leave the request unresolved. Turn-level scores do not show this pattern.With multi-turn evaluation, you set the evaluation level of a run to score each turn or the conversation as a whole. Conversation-level evaluators, such as task completion, customer satisfaction, coherence, groundedness and tool use quality, find problems like incomplete task resolution, user frustration and tool-call regressions. You provide conversation data as JSONL with a full messages array, including tool calls and tool definitions, and run the evaluation with the Foundry SDK.Learn more.
